name: Sneddon Syndrome

criteria.description: Generalized livedo racemosa (widespread, irregular, non-reversible reticular pattern on skin)
Cerebrovascular events (TIA or stroke, particularly in young adults)
Skin biopsy showing non-inflammatory thrombotic vasculopathy of dermal vessels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Combination of generalized livedo racemosa plus cerebrovascular events (TIA or stroke). Skin biopsy demonstrating thrombotic vasculopathy of medium-sized arteries is confirmatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Two forms: (1) antiphospholipid antibody-positive (~40-50%, overlap with APS), and (2) seronegative. The livedo pattern is typically racemosa (irregular, broken rings) not reticularis (regular, complete rings).

pathognomonic.symptomName: Livedo racemosa (widespread, persistent, irregular reticular skin pattern)
pathognomonic.notes: Widespread, irregular, broken-ring pattern on trunk and extremities; does not resolve with warming (unlike livedo reticularis)

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent cerebrovascular events in young adults
pathognomonic.notes: Ischemic strokes or TIAs; mean age at first event ~30-40 years

common.notes: Subcortical vascular dementia pattern from multiple infarcts
May be related to renal artery involvement

occasional.symptomName: Visual disturbances (amaurosis fugax, visual field defects)

laboratory: Antiphospholipid antibodies positive in ~40-50% (anticardiolipin, lupus anticoagulant, anti-beta2GP1)
imaging: MRI brain: multiple infarcts (often subcortical white matter and periventricular, medium vessel territory)
MRA/CTA: stenosis or occlusion of medium-sized intracranial arteries
Renal artery Doppler: may show stenosis
genetic: CECR1/ADA2 gene mutations (adenosine deaminase 2 deficiency) reported in some familial cases
Rare familial autosomal dominant pattern described
other: Skin biopsy (deep punch or wedge): endothelial proliferation and thrombosis of medium-sized arteries in deep dermis/subcutis
Conventional angiography: beading/occlusion of medium cerebral arteries
Transcranial Doppler: may show stenosis of intracranial vessels

distinguishingFeatures: APS requires persistently positive aPL antibodies (by definition)
APS may have venous thrombosis (DVT/PE) in addition to arterial
~40-50% of Sneddon patients have aPL, representing overlap
SLE has positive ANA, anti-dsDNA, multisystem involvement
SLE may have nephritis, serositis, malar rash
Susac has BRAO and hearing loss as part of clinical triad
Susac has central corpus callosum lesions on MRI
PAN has systemic vasculitis with necrotizing inflammation
PAN affects medium arteries with microaneurysms

redFlags: Acute stroke in young patient with livedo racemosa (do not dismiss as benign livedo reticularis)
Progressive cognitive decline suggesting multi-infarct dementia
Cardiac valve disease with embolic risk
New-onset hypertension in young patient (consider renal artery involvement)
references: Sneddon IB. Cerebro-vascular lesions and livedo reticularis. Br J Dermatol. 1965;77:180-185.
Francois B, et al. Sneddon's syndrome: a comprehensive review. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2021;16:329.
Wu S, et al. Sneddon syndrome: a comprehensive clinical review. Semin Arthritis Rheum. 2014;44(2):158-164.
